436 | def restrict_queryset_to_visible(
437 |     queryset: QuerySet[ModelT],
438 |     user: User | None,
439 |     perm: str,
440 | ) -> QuerySet[ModelT]:
441 |     """
442 |     Restrict ``queryset`` to the rows ``user`` may see with ``perm``.
443 | 
444 |     Delegates the visibility check to the database as a
445 |     ``WHERE id IN (subquery)`` rather than materializing the full
446 |     permitted-id set into a Python collection first: a caller that only
447 |     needs to check a small handful of rows (a resolved-id list, a few
448 |     RAG-neighbour candidate ids) never pays for scanning or holding the
449 |     installation's entire taxonomy in memory to do it.
450 | 
451 |     Returns ``queryset`` unchanged for user_is_unrestricted(user); every
452 |     other case is delegated to ``permitted_object_ids`` rather than
453 |     re-deciding the ordering here.
454 |     """
455 |     if user_is_unrestricted(user):
456 |         return queryset
457 |     return queryset.filter(pk__in=permitted_object_ids(user, queryset.model, perm))
458 |

460 | def permitted_document_ids(
461 |     user: User | None,
462 |     *,
463 |     perm: str = "view_document",
464 |     include_deleted: bool = False,
465 | ) -> QuerySet[int]:
466 |     """
467 |     Document-specific convenience wrapper around ``permitted_object_ids``.
468 |     Return a queryset of document IDs the user has ``perm`` on (default
469 |     ``"view_document"``). By default limited to non-deleted documents; pass
470 |     ``include_deleted=True`` for callers that need to check permission on
471 |     soft-deleted documents (e.g. trash restore). This intentionally avoids
472 |     ``get_objects_for_user`` to keep the subquery small and index-friendly.
473 |     """
474 |     return permitted_object_ids(user, Document, perm, include_deleted=include_deleted)

589 | def get_objects_for_user_owner_aware(
590 |     user: User | None,
591 |     perms: str | list[str],
592 |     Model: Any,
593 |     *,
594 |     include_deleted: bool = False,
595 | ) -> QuerySet[Any]:
596 |     """
597 |     Returns objects the user owns, are unowned, or has explicit perms.
598 |     When include_deleted is True, soft-deleted items are also included.
599 | 
600 |     Legacy slow path (guardian-backed, O(n) style permission resolution).
601 |     Most queryset-filtering call sites have migrated onto
602 |     ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this function
603 |     is kept because production callers still remain. Several callers remain
604 |     across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/`` --
605 |     grep for this function name before removing it.
606 |     """
607 |     manager = (
608 |         Model.global_objects
609 |         if include_deleted and hasattr(Model, "global_objects")
610 |         else Model.objects
611 |     )
612 | 
613 |     objects_owned = manager.filter(owner=user)
614 |     objects_unowned = manager.filter(owner__isnull=True)
615 |     objects_with_perms = get_objects_for_user(
616 |         user=user,
617 |         perms=perms,
618 |         klass=manager.all(),
619 |         accept_global_perms=False,
620 |     )
621 |     return objects_owned | objects_unowned | objects_with_perms

observations.claim: The notes action accepts GET, POST, and DELETE as a detail action and selects PaperlessNotePermissions for the action.

observations.subject: current caller
observations.claim: The action binds the caller from request.user; PaperlessNotePermissions rejects absent or unauthenticated users.

observations.subject: URL/detail pk
observations.claim: The action fetches Document by the detail pk, with owner and notes loaded; the object check and returned notes are tied to that fetched document.

observations.subject: GET endpoint-level permissions
observations.claim: Before the action, GET requires authenticated model-level documents.view_note and documents.view_document permissions.

observations.subject: GET document-level control
observations.claim: The action checks view_document through has_perms_owner_aware; that helper allows when the document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the caller has the object permission.

observations.subject: GET
observations.claim: On the passing path, GET serializes the fetched document and returns its notes.

observations.subject: ownership branches
observations.claim: Document ownership is unspecified. An unowned document or one owned by the caller bypasses the object grant; a document owned by another principal requires the caller's object-level view_document permission. Supplied facts do not select a branch.

observations.claim: The notes action accepts POST as a detail action and selects PaperlessNotePermissions for the action.

observations.subject: current caller
observations.claim: The caller is request.user; the permission class requires authentication, and a created note records that caller as its user.

observations.subject: URL/detail pk
observations.object: Document fetched by pk and new Note.document
observations.claim: The action fetches the addressed Document by pk, checks permissions on that same object, and creates the Note with document=doc.

observations.subject: POST endpoint-level permissions
observations.claim: Before the action, POST requires authenticated model-level documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document permissions.

observations.subject: POST document-level controls
observations.claim: POST first passes the common owner-aware view_document check and then an owner-aware change_document check. Each owner-aware check passes if the document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the corresponding object permission is present.

observations.subject: POST
observations.claim: On the passing path, POST creates a Note attached to the fetched document with request.data['note'] and request.user, updates the document, and returns the document's notes.

observations.subject: ownership and grant branches
observations.claim: Document ownership and object grants are unspecified. For an unowned document or caller-owned document, both object checks pass without grants. For another principal's document, view_document and change_document object permissions are both needed by this path; missing view denies at the common check and missing change denies before creation.
